question: Which statement best describes Core table structure?
options: These group rows by role: <thead> holds the column-header row(s), <tbody> holds the data rows, and <tfoot> holds summary/aggregate rows (totals). They improve semantics, let you style or scroll the body independently of a sticky header, and (historically) help printing repeat headers across pages. The browser will imply a <tbody> even if you omit it.

A table is built from rows (<tr>) that contain cells. Data cells use <td>; header cells use <th>. The browser builds a grid by aligning cells across rows. Every table should describe a two-dimensional relationship between row and column headers and their data values — if your content isn't really a grid of related values, a table is the wrong element.

A <th> is a header cell, announced differently from data cells. The scope attribute tells assistive tech which cells a header applies to: scope="col" for a column header, scope="row" for a row header. Without scope, screen readers may guess wrong on complex tables. Set scope on every <th> in any non-trivial table so each data cell is correctly associated with its headers.

question: Which statement best describes thead, tbody, and tfoot?
options: colspan makes a cell span multiple columns; rowspan makes it span multiple rows — used for grouped headers or merged values. The numbers must keep the grid rectangular: a row that omits cells because an earlier rowspan covers them is correct, but mismatched spans produce a broken, inaccessible layout. Keep spanning minimal and consistent.

Wide tables overflow on small screens. Common patterns: wrap in a scroll container (overflow-x:auto) so the table scrolls horizontally, or restyle to stacked cards with CSS.
